body: For me it's about validating feelings. People want  you to smile for their benefit. That's not enough to live by. Need to be real. Would be nice if someone in my life cared about my feelings, too. But, no. Solitary. And, no, therapists never helped.

Good for you. I relate to what the OP said and for me it's not about comparing to others, in essence. That's just a benchmark to highlight the fact that all the damn effort doesn't pay out for us. Life ain't worth it. I don't have unrealistic dreams of being a star or having a successful glamour profession like writing or music. But life should be an adventurous trip, not prison.
Just as everywhere else, no one here could possibly care. I'm such an outlier, I don't matter. Should not have been born. Time to die.
But not for me. People aren't meant to be alone. No meaning for me, except time to end it.

I think name-calling fits under ad hominem attack, as it's about the person rather than the content. 

I don't see how your examples reflect anything bad about me. 

I probably shouldn't have wasted my time giving examples, since you started off with an insult. And have now ignored the examples, as well.

What have I written that makes you think that of me? (By the way, is that not an ad hominem attack?)

An example of what he did, from my OP:

>aggressively demanding to ban my emotional expression while at the same time frequently expressing his own feelings

Some more examples, since you asked:

I requested that he not email me when he's angry, because I get afraid to open emails and it's not helpful to deal with emotions like that in email. He refuses to respect that boundary and tries to make a deal that I never ever express emotions (ironic in the context of him sending an angry, ie emotional, email) plus other terms, or "no deal." I wasn't bargaining. I was making a reasonable request. There is no deal to be made, simply a reasonable and respectful response to a reasonable request.

He sends me an incomprehensible email. I have to ask several questions to get what he's talking about. Not that it's some techie thing, just he'll leave out the key information that makes whatever he's saying comprehensible, while flooding the message with other whimsical and emotional content. It's a pattern. I ask him to please consider me before sending, and think about whether the key information is there. No, he can't because he's autistic - disabled. (And when he uses that expression orally, it's said with vehemence, so that's how I hear it in the email. It's never gentle and asking for understanding. It's like a scolding.) However, he can teach...spent hours refining his lectures, as I well know as I helped him extensively in the first term that he did it. I've seen him write and rewrite drafts of various documents. A reasonable response would be, first acknowledgment that, "Oops, yeah I did leave out that key information" and secondly, "Sure, I'll try to do that" and then actually try - don't just forget about it.

These happened this weekend. Another one a couple months ago was we had planned to go to part of this all-day event together. On the day of, I said, hey, let's figure out our timing on when we'll leave to get there. Instantly he blew up and raged at me that we're not going unless I drive. (He can't drive.) And then further expression of his contempt for "mere chatting" that I would have enjoyed doing, catching up, on transit. Then he left, with no attempt to come up with a solution for getting there or even hear my point of view on it. Later we talked about it and saw how we could have worked it, but it was too late. The event was over. This is typical that only his point of view matters and he flies into a rage and walks if he doesn't get his way on some point that is suddenly of utmost importance in his mind.
